title: Normalisation
summary: Refactor a messy spreadsheet-table into 1NF, 2NF and 3NF, and move the data across.

steps.title: Why one big table hurts
body: The box office's spreadsheet became one table:
order_id  customer_name  customer_email  show_title         show_date   seats     price_each
1         Ana Sousa      ana@mail.test   The Tempest Below  2026-12-04  A1,A2     3000
3         Ana Sousa      ana@mail.test   Gaslight Choir     2026-12-11  B1,B2,B3  2500
- **Update anomaly:** Ana changes her email. Miss one of her rows and she has two emails.
- **Insertion anomaly:** you can't record a new show until someone buys a ticket for it.
- **Deletion anomaly:** delete Chloe's only order and you've forgotten Chloe exists.
- **Multi-valued cells:** "who has seat B2?" needs string searching, and `LIKE '%B2%'` also matches `B21`.
**Normalisation** splits a table so **each fact is stored once**.

steps.prompt: Ben appears in two orders. An UPDATE changes his email in only one of them. Which problem is this?

steps.title: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF
body: The **normal forms** are a checklist, each building on the last:
**1NF: one value per cell, no repeating groups.** `seats = 'A1,A2'` breaks it; so do columns `seat1, seat2, seat3`. Fix: a separate `order_seats` table with one row per seat.
**2NF: no partial dependencies.** In a table keyed by `(order_id, seat)`, a column like `customer_email` depends on `order_id` alone, not the whole key. Move it to a table keyed by `order_id`.
**3NF: no transitive dependencies.** In `orders`, `show_date` depends on `show_title`, which depends on the order. Facts about a show belong in `shows`, referenced by `show_id`.
The one-line summary people quote: every non-key column depends on *the key, the whole key, and nothing but the key*.
> **In practice:** design to 3NF, then denormalise deliberately (for a reporting table, say) when you have a measured reason.

steps.title: Refactor 1: customers
prompt: Start pulling facts out of `orders_flat`. Create **`customers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE)`** and fill it with **each customer once**, using INSERT ... SELECT (let `id` number itself).
Table: `orders_flat(order_id, customer_name, customer_email, show_title, show_date, seats, price_each)`
solution: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
INSERT INTO customers (name, email)
SELECT DISTINCT customer_name, customer_email FROM orders_flat;

steps.title: Refactor 3: orders
prompt: Create **`orders(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), show_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES shows(id))`**, and fill it from `orders_flat`, keeping the original **order ids**. Look up the new customer and show ids with joins (by email and by title).
Tables: `orders_flat(order_id, customer_name, customer_email, show_title, show_date, seats, price_each)`, plus your `customers` and `shows`.
solution: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), show_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES shows(id));
INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, show_id)
SELECT f.order_id, c.id, s.id
FROM orders_flat AS f
JOIN customers AS c ON c.email = f.customer_email
JOIN shows AS s ON s.title = f.show_title;
setup: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

steps.title: Refactor 4: one seat per row
prompt: The last 1NF violation: `seats` holds lists like `'B1,B2,B3'`. Create **`order_seats(order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), seat TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (order_id, seat))`** and fill it with **one row per seat**.
Splitting text needs a recursive CTE: peel off the part before the first comma, then repeat on the rest.
Tables: `orders_flat(order_id, customer_name, customer_email, show_title, show_date, seats, price_each)`, plus your `customers`, `shows` and `orders`.
solution: CREATE TABLE order_seats (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), seat TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (order_id, seat));
WITH RECURSIVE split(order_id, seat, rest) AS (
SELECT order_id, '', seats || ',' FROM orders_flat
UNION ALL
SELECT order_id, substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1), substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1)
FROM split WHERE rest <> ''
INSERT INTO order_seats (order_id, seat)
SELECT order_id, seat FROM split WHERE seat <> '';

hints: Anchor: `SELECT order_id, '', seats || ',' FROM orders_flat` (a trailing comma makes every seat end the same way).
Step: `substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1)` is the next seat and `substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1)` is what's left; stop `WHERE rest <> ''`.
Insert the CTE rows `WHERE seat <> ''` (the anchor row has an empty seat).
